question: If $\left|\begin{matrix}\alpha&3&4\\ 1&2&1\\ 1&4&1\end{matrix}\right|=0$ , then the value of $\alpha$ is
explanation:
**Step 1:** Expand the determinant along the first row: $\alpha(2(1) - 1(4)) - 3(1(1) - 1(1)) + 4(1(4) - 2(1)) = 0$.
**Step 2:** Simplify each component: $\alpha(2 - 4) - 3(1 - 1) + 4(4 - 2) = 0 \implies \alpha(-2) - 3(0) + 4(2) = 0$. This gives $-2\alpha + 8 = 0 \implies 2\alpha = 8 \implies \alpha = 4$.
